output.name: *Ornesk* — "the Waiting Hook"
output.myth: When the first frost comes, the stew-pots come in from the yard and go up on the hook, and that is why Ornesk rises then. Ennu bent it first from a rib of old whale, so the pot would hang over the fire and not in the wind. Aun saw it from the cliff and wanted it for his own. He took it down to the Upper Sea to cook a fish too big for the islands, and the pot went with him, the hook on its string. Hesk counted the pots that night and found one short. Tavo laughed and blew the pot away over the water, so hard he near fell out of the sky, and it came down west beside the Hat the Gale Kept. Up in the north, the Wind-Gull watched the whole business from above and said nothing, as gulls do. The hook stayed in the sky with its tip still empty, waiting. Grandmothers say a kettle must always be hung again. Mind your own pots, and you will not need Aun to mend them.
output.finding: From the Wind-Gull in the north, drop one hand-span (about 20°) straight south and you will find the Pot Hook.
